actions_taken: migration 003 adds a settings table (key -> JSON) with db.settings; the repository returns unknown on purpose and every reader parses it with the zod schema it already has, so a hand-edited row fails where it is read

C01: zotero:listCollections, zotero:getImportScope and zotero:setImportScope; ZoteroImporter.import takes collections[] and filters the one item fetch against the union of their keys, so several picks are one import and a paper filed twice is seen once. zotero:import with no scope of its own falls back to the remembered picks -- absent means 'use the picks', an explicitly empty list means the whole library

the picker falls back to the collections the last import mirrored when Zotero is not running, and says so: Zotero serves its local API only while open, so a live-only picker is empty exactly when someone opens the app to read

C02: NotesFolder owns the four-step change -- remember, swap the allow-list, purge the notes from the folder no longer in use, re-import. SwappableRoots is the allow-list object every path check holds, so a change reaches rrfile://, the pipeline and the importer at once rather than whichever was built first

the purge is a hard delete (documents.purge cascades; links and external_references have no FK and are cleared in the same transaction). A tombstone would bring the rows back the moment anything listed deleted documents. It also runs at startup, which is what clears the twelve stranded corpus rows that answered every click with 403 Forbidden

the renderer gets the folder's *name*, never its path, and corpus:chooseFolder takes no payload -- a channel that accepted a path would be an arbitrary-directory read wearing a preference's clothes. A test asserts no response contains the folder's path

C03: the activity bar's four glyphs carry their names as rendered text; the bar widened from 48px to 68px. The test measures a layout box and a computed font size, because 'the string is in the DOM' is true of font-size: 0
errors: the build broke with 'Unterminated string literal' in out/main/index.js: electron-vite appends its CommonJS shim after the last match of a static-import regex over the whole bundle, and a log string ending in the bare word 'import' followed by another string literal matches it, so the shim landed inside a string. iteration_hint: the queue: questions with a stored status, a stored order, a kept discard reason, typed edges
actions_taken: migration 004 adds `questions`. `ordinal` is the hand-order and nothing derives it -- sorting by created_at or importance would replace a judgement about what to do next with a fact about when something was typed

the CHECK (status <> 'discarded' OR discarded_reason IS NOT NULL) is deliberate: discarding is not deleting, the reason is the residue worth keeping, and the schema refuses a reasonless discard so no path -- repository, IPC or raw SQL -- can produce one. The test proves all three paths refuse it

questions.reorder(ids) takes a *subset*: it collects the ordinals those ids already occupy, sorts them, and hands them back out in the new order, so a drag inside one filtered list cannot disturb the questions interleaved around it

Q04 uses the existing links table with sourceType 'question' -- no second relationship mechanism. question:attach exists only so both endpoints are checked to exist before the edge is written; an edge to a document not in the library is a broken link the moment it is created, and the test asserts the refusal
question:update refuses status: 'discarded' rather than accepting it with a null reason: routing the transition through a channel with no field for a reason would lose it
'question' joins LinkableEntityType and EntityResolver.describe, so a question resolves in references, peek and the graph like anything else
errors: the Q01 order assertion was first written over questions in insertion order, which would have passed on an implementation with no stored ordinal at all; rewritten to reorder into an arrangement no field sorts into

iteration_hint: the queue panel: a grip, a drag, and an order that outlives the process
actions_taken: renderer/queue-panel.tsx: a questions sidebar behind a new activity-bar button. The list is rendered in the order the main process returned and nothing in the view ever re-sorts it -- a drop sends the new id order to question:reorder and then takes back what the database says it is, so the view never keeps an arrangement that was not accepted

reordering has two ways in: pointer-drag from the grip, and ArrowUp/ArrowDown while the grip has focus. A grip you can only drag is a grip some people cannot use, and both paths go through the same moveWithin and commit

the order on screen is mirrored in a ref as well as in state. Committing from inside a setState updater would have sent the reorder twice under StrictMode, because React is free to run an updater more than once; computing the next order first and handing it to setQuestions keeps the updater pure

the E2E drags with a real pointer over CDP rather than calling the channel: the criterion is that a person can arrange the queue, and a spec that invoked question:reorder would pass with no grip on the screen. Three questions are dragged into an order that is neither creation order nor its reverse nor alphabetical, then a second Electron process is launched over the same library
mutation-checked: making questions.reorder a no-op fails both [Q02] tests and the [Q01] stored-order test
errors: the first drag helper aimed at the near quarter of the target row, which is short of its midpoint, so dragging *downwards* never crossed the threshold that swaps two rows. It aims past the midpoint in the direction of travel now

openQueue clicked the activity button blind, which closed the sidebar in the second process: the workspace layout restores the sidebars that were open, so the panel was already up. It toggles only when hidden

actions_taken: migration 005 journal_entries is keyed by the ISO date rather than a minted id: there is exactly one entry per day, and a link to 'what I did on the 20th' should mean that day and survive the entry being cleared and written again

the CHECK on markdown refuses the empty string, and journal.write() with blank markdown deletes the row. 'No entry' and 'an empty entry' are the same fact; a calendar able to tell them apart would be showing a difference that does not exist. Asserted three ways: the channel answers null, the row is gone, and a hand-written INSERT of '' throws

J02 is a pure, clock-free function in the renderer -- calendarCells takes today as an argument, so the test can stand anywhere in the year. The two rules with the off-by-one in them are asserted from both sides: three idle days stay three bubbles and four fold into one marker, and today never folds and splits a run, which can drop a fold below the threshold on both sides

J03 reuses links with sourceType 'journal' and type journal-entry-advances-question. journal:advancesQuestion checks both ends exist first: an edge from a day nobody wrote on, or to a question not in the queue, is broken the moment it is written

the panel exists because the criteria are integration-level and would be satisfied by a feature no one can reach: JournalView renders the calendar from calendarCells, saves on blur, and offers the question picker only once the day has an entry. A short e2e drives it, because a save that never fires is invisible to a test that calls the channel
errors: the [J03] refusal test used a 22-character placeholder id, which the router rejects as INVALID_REQUEST before the handler ever looks it up -- so the test was asserting the id format, not the existence check. Ids are <prefix>_<26 chars>; both placeholders are well-formed now

actions_taken: apps/desktop/src/main/agents/workspace.ts: AgentWorkspace, one root, and the only path by which anything writes on the librarian's behalf. Every write resolves through it; there is no second door for accept to use later

containment is decided twice because the string test is not the test that matters. `notes/x.md` where `notes` is a symlink out of the root is inside the workspace lexically and outside it after open(2), so the second check runs realpath on the deepest ancestor that exists and re-appends what does not, which resolves every link the OS would walk without requiring the leaf to be there
the refusal is logged at warn with the path that was asked for, so a run that keeps trying to escape is visible rather than merely thwarted

runDirectory mints <root>/.runs/<id> through the same resolve, so a run id carrying ../ is refused like any other escape. list() skips .runs: a proposal is in the workspace but is not yet part of what the workspace holds

tests/integration/agent-workspace.test.ts drives five different escapes against a real temp filesystem with real planted symlinks -- climbing, absolute, symlinked directory, symlinked existing file, and a NUL byte -- and asserts both that nothing landed outside and that the attempt was logged
next_action: A01: spawn a headless claude with --system-prompt-file and stream stream-json progress, built on AgentWorkspace.

actions_taken: probed the installed CLI rather than trusting the doc: --system-prompt-file exists in 2.1.220 and validates the file before anything else happens, so a missing prompt fails without a network call. The help text lists only --system-prompt and --append-system-prompt; the -file forms are real but appear only inside the --bare description

recorded the fixture instead of writing one. One real `claude --output-format stream-json` run of the librarian's own prompt over a two-document corpus written to disagree with itself. It found the contradiction, cited both with [[wikilinks]] and wrote one note -- which is A06-A08 behaving before either was built. 47 events covering every kind the runner must survive: system/init, thinking_tokens, hook_started, assistant text/thinking/tool_use, user tool_result, rate_limit_event, result/success

two mechanical redactions and no others: home paths, and the init event's slash_commands/skills/plugins inventories, which describe the laptop it was recorded on rather than the stream contract. tests/fixtures/agents/README.md says so

agents/stream.ts parses what it recognises and returns null for the rest. An unknown event is a line from a newer CLI, not an error -- enumerating what to ignore is a list that goes stale. One assistant line can carry several blocks, so parseStreamLine returns an array: a two-tool-call turn that reported one call would be a silent undercount

agents/prompt.ts makes the remit data. Each capability is one line appended only when enabled, so switching directions off removes the sentence rather than adding one that argues against it -- which is the only form A09 can be asserted in

agents/runner.ts spawns with --system-prompt-file (replaces, where --append- would leave Claude Code's instructions in front of ours), --output-format stream-json (a --print run is a black box indistinguishable from a hang), --tools limited to the crawl set, and --strict-mcp-config with no config, so there is no retrieval anywhere in the path by construction
the runner writes its system prompt through AgentWorkspace, not with writeFile. Giving the runner a privileged path of its own would have put an exception in the boundary on day one

tests/fixtures/agents/fake-claude.mjs replays the recording as a real child process and writes the argv it was handed to disk, so the spawn is asserted rather than assumed -- a runner that silently dropped --system-prompt-file would still have streamed. It chunks at 3000 bytes to land splits mid-line, because one recorded event is 20 kB of file content
errors: A09 and A11 now have passing tagged tests that cover only their first halves.
